about.title: Monte Sereno Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Monte Sereno is a small place, home to about 3,556 people in Santa Clara County. When a life is lost here, the absence is felt on quiet streets and in familiar routines. Public records show the city recorded six injury collisions in 2024, with seven people hurt and no traffic deaths, and most reported crashes clustered on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. along Saratoga Los Gatos Road, Route 9, La Rinconada Drive and Winchester Boulevard. Yet wrongful death claims are not limited to the roadway. A fall on unsafe property, a medical error, a defective product or a crash on a neighboring highway can all leave a family with the same questions. California law gives a spouse, domestic partner and children the first right to bring a civil claim, and sets a two-year deadline from the date of death, shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive simply listens, then connects you at no cost with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency. You decide whether to move forward.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general limit is two years from the date of death, and a claim involving a city, county or state road like Route 9 must be presented much sooner. Early guidance protects your options.

items.question: Monte Sereno reported no traffic deaths in 2024. Does that mean a wrongful death claim here is unusual?
items.answer: Low counts reflect a small community, not the limits of the law. Many Monte Sereno residents commute along Saratoga Los Gatos Road and Winchester Boulevard into neighboring cities, and a fatal event elsewhere in Santa Clara County can still be pursued from home. Deaths tied to medical care, property hazards or products are also covered by the same statute.

items.question: Do we have to wait for the criminal case to finish before filing?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action with its own two-year deadline, and it can move forward whether or not charges are filed. An attorney can also help preserve evidence that a criminal investigation may not gather for your family's purposes.

items.question: What if the death involved a government vehicle or a poorly maintained public road?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity in California follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and a formal claim must usually be presented before a lawsuit. Because Route 9 and other corridors in Monte Sereno are publicly maintained, this comes up more often than families expect. Speaking with an attorney soon after the loss helps avoid missing that window.
